corrections.ruling: C (round 2): the rice card names «ٹماٹر» alone — «… گوشت یا مرغی، ٹماٹر اور مسالوں (…) کے ساتھ …». Two readers of two read «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی» (round 1’s A) as the side chutney, and the reference’s own article defines it so: a misreading of what goes into the dish outweighs the loss of the form ’sauce’, which is charged under accuracy. B refused under P16 (no entry; a native wording exists); D refused: «مسالا» beside «مسالوں» in the same list reads as the spices. «ٹماٹر» is an English loan with its own Urdu headword and gender (Rekhta, Origin English, Noun Masculine) and no native competitor: P16 is satisfied by the headword, as N126 ruled for «کیتلی»; entered verified as «ٹماٹر» (addendum to round 2). Round 1’s pending entry «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی» is withdrawn (never in the termbase); a real tomato chutney on a later page is still «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی».
corrections.evidence: ur.wikipedia exact phrase «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی» 11 pages (stage 1, s1-web.json, HTTP 200, 2026-10-15): its own article defines a subcontinental chutney («چٹنیوں کی ایک قسم»), but the kushari article lists it among the cooked parts of a dish of pasta, rice and lentils — the cooking-sauce sense the source means (EN ’tomato sauce’, AR «صلصة الطماطم»). B’s words are loans with no termbase entry (P16: no loan where a native wording exists). C says less than both sources. «ٹماٹر» is the naturalised everyday word with no native competitor; no dictionary page was read for it at this stage. ROUND 2: the on-r1 reader too read it as the sweet-sour table chutney (item 5, moderate): two readers of two. ADDENDUM (proof on r2, should-fix 3): rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-tamaatar (HTTP 200, 2026-10-15): «ٹَماٹَر — Origin : English — Noun, Masculine — tomato», Urdu «اسم، مذکر ایک سبزی …»; ur.wikipedia «ٹماٹر» 171 pages (HTTP 200).
